notes:
Summary: evaluation for repo-aware IDE copilot. Primary ask: low-latency streaming completions inside VS Code with accurate repo context and strong residency guarantees.

Timeline / Activities:
- 2026-01-05: Intro call (AE Jordan, SE Maya). Discussed architecture and target metrics. Gmail thread gt_20260105_skeinforge_poc.
- 2026-01-12: Technical deep-dive with eng leads. Fireflies id ff_20260128_skeinforge_poc_call referenced for follow-up clips.
- 2026-01-20: POC kickoff. Provided sample repo snapshot (monorepo ~70GB, many small packages).
- 2026-02-02: First POC results — embedding accuracy good, but tail latency spikes when cold-starting repo shards. Ticketed as INF-3214.
- 2026-02-10: Security review kickoff; asked for KMS/HSM options and audit log retention details.

Technical requirements & notes:
- Retrieval model: want per-repo and per-branch vector indices; must support per-commit pinning for reproducing suggestions.
- Chunking: aggressive semantic chunking preferred (200-800 tokens) plus overlap for cross-file references; need ability to tune chunk size per repo.
- Vector DB: evaluating two options — Redwood-managed vectors in VPC vs customer-hosted (self-managed Milvus/FAISS). Residency requirement: index and raw code must stay in customer VPC / on-prem for enterprise tier.
- Latency: 95th percentile < 120ms for token streaming in editor; cold-start allowable up to 300ms for first request after long idle. Throughput: dozens of concurrent devs per repo.
- Model / versioning: pin to a model family for deterministic completions; fallback policy required (smaller quantized family) when capacity constrained. Need rollout capability for model updates and A/B evaluation across cohorts.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching for file context and local developer workspace preferred; suggestion to leverage local-edits-based ephemeral cache to reduce roundtrips.
- Security: SSO/SAML integration mandatory, audit logs for every retrieval call, retention controls (90/365/never) configurable per customer policy.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for dedicated pools for hot repos, but wants Optimize toolkit recommendations to reduce token costs (batching, quantization).

POC deliverables requested:
- Latency heatmap for per-repo vector shards (cold vs warm).
- Proof of concept showing per-branch index isolation and commit-level vector snapshots.
- Pricing estimate for private deployment (VPC) and for dedicated GPU pool to meet 95p latency SLO. Deck: drive://redwood-sales/decks/skeinforge-poc-pricing-v2.pdf

Customer quotes / paraphrases:
- "We need completions that understand our mono-repo context and don't leak other customers' code."
- "If we can't host vectors in our VPC we can't move forward — residency is non-negotiable for some customers."

Next steps (short):
- Deliver the POC latency report and recommended vector DB topology by 2026-02-21.
- Legal to confirm data residency SLA language; coordinate with Redwood legal.
- Schedule SOC2 gap review with Security on 2026-02-18.

Internal notes for AE/SE:
- Prioritize demo of per-branch pinning and commit snapshots; show model pin rollback flow.
- Show Optimize recommendations: batching windows that maintain latency SLO for editor streaming.
- Track INF-3278 (request for HSM/KMS integration specification).
